pages.text: A weak acid HA and its salt A⁻ hold a pH set by their ratio: pH = pKa + log₁₀([A⁻]/[HA]) (Henderson-Hasselbalch). Added acid or base only shifts the ratio a little - as long as there is plenty of both. The buffer capacity, 4r/(1 + r)², is best at a ratio of 1.
$(thing)Set$(): Salt to acid ratio.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Mixing error: the ratio is off by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): No buffering left: the ratio is too far from 1.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A better buffer is made faster (less correcting).
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)pH: pH = pKa + log₁₀([A⁻]/[HA])$(br)Buffer capacity: β = 4r/(1 + r)²
